title: Beta launch ops — mental models & telemetry diary (working)
content:
Purpose and scope:

This is a scratch diary of mental models, lightweight telemetry patterns, and ceremony drafts for small-scale beta launches (customer-facing gated releases). The goal: provide a practical checklist and signal lexicon that PM/Prod-Eng/SRE/Support can use without heavy ceremony — suitable for teams shipping a new routing/experiment change that touches the Redwood Console and API paths.

Audience:
- PMs owning feature activation
- Console engineers who configure exposure slices
- Oncall SRE and Product Ops
- Solutions/SE for early customer handoffs
- Support for customer-facing comms

High-level mental model (one-liners):
- Start very small and observable: safety of a beta is proportional to how quickly you can see and reverse the change.
- Prefer signal diversity over single aggregated metric: combine telemetry, qualitative feedback, and simple user-facing checks.
- OODA loop: Observe -> Orient -> Decide -> Act. Shorten it by reducing noise and making actions explicit.

Decision ladder (quick):
1) Immediate stop (30 min): severity: user-facing errors >1% or latency p50 jumps >150% on beta slice, or any P0 security/compliance alert.
2) Scale back (2–6 hours): slow drift in quality/engagement signals, cost burn > projection by 30% tied to beta routing.
3) Continue (daily): no material deviations, proceed to broaden slices per schedule.

Telemetry radar (signals we care about, prioritized):
- Health signals (must have): 
  - 5xx error rate (per-route, per-model) — alert threshold: >0.5% sustained for 10m on slice
  - P95 latency (token generation) — alert: >2x baseline for 5m
  - Throttles/Rate-limit hits — any increase on beta slice
- Economics signals: 
  - Cost per 1k tokens on beta vs control — alert if >30% deviation
  - GPU utilization and queue depth for dedicated pools serving beta models
- Quality signals (observational):
  - Model-specific regressions (eval-run on sample prompts) daily delta >3% failure rate
  - Human-rated quality checks (seeded prompts) — weekly metric and rapid check sample in first 48 hours
- UX/customer signals:
  - Support tickets referencing beta feature or model behaviors (tagging in SupportDB) — any mention within 24h = human review
  - Crash reports / browser console errors if frontend involved
- Behavioral signals:
  - Click-through/engagement on features behind the beta toggle compared to expected baseline

Quick telemetry design patterns (practical):
- Use a tiny, persistent sample of real traffic (10–50 reqs/min) to run a parallel evaluator that checks for quality regressions on seeded prompts. Keep this separate from user slices to avoid contamination.
- Tag every metric with slice_id, model_version, region, and rollout_ticket to make queryable slices in the Console.
- Build a small dashboard (1–2 panels) that pairs latency/error + a quality proxy (eval pass rate) — we look at both before making scale decisions.
- Synthetic probes: do not rely solely on customer traffic in first 24h. Run synthetic sequences that exercise edge-case behaviors (long contexts, function calls, streaming).

Stakeholder ceremony (lightweight):
- Pre-start (T-48h): Dry-run comms, ensure SRE runbook link is live, owner assigned for 24/7 on-call window; confirm rollback playbook.
- Kick (T0): brief async post in #prod-rollouts with rollout_ticket, targets, and 'stop conditions'. Include link to small dashboard and steward contact.
- Pulse checks: cadence at T+15m, T+60m, then every 4h for day1. Short note: "status: OK / Noise / Action" only. Keep updates terse.
- Escalation: if stop condition met, steward posts to #prod-rollouts + @oncall-sre, triggers automated rollback if precondition satisfied.

Runbook snippets (to copy into ops tool):
- To stop: switch route weight to 0 for slice_id=xxx in Console -> routing -> override -> commit. Confirm downstream queues drained for 2x expected max-latency window.
- To scale back: reduce weight to 10% and enable fallback-model variant. Leave short note in ticket.
- Post-mortem snapshot: capture last 3 hours of traces, top 20 failing prompts from seeded set, error logs, and diff of model params (if quantization/variant change).

Sample signal thresholds (starter heuristics):
- Error spikes: >0.5% sustained for 10m OR 2x baseline for 5m.
- Latency: P95 > 2x baseline for 5m OR P50 > 1.5x for 10m.
- Cost: daily spend for beta > 150% projected in first 24h.
- Quality: seeded-eval failure delta +3 percentage points vs control in 1h window.

Customer-facing considerations:
- If beta is customer-specific, proactively notify account team and create a shared Slack channel for first 72h.
- For privacy/sensitive customers, ensure Private deployment checklist (KMS/HSM audit) is completed before starting.

Open questions / tradeoffs we are still deciding: 
- Do we allow automated rollback on quality regressions (yes for health/cost, maybe for quality; requires human verification)?
- How many seeded prompts are 'enough' to detect subtle regressions without too much noise? (current thinking: ~300 diverse prompts, flagged by model-type).
- Should we gate by model family or feature surface (e.g., tool-calling enabled) — prefer gating by feature surface first.

Notes to self and todo (next 7 days):
- Build a tiny "beta pulse" viz with 4 panels (errors, latency, cost-per-token, seeded-eval pass) — owner: Liam. Due: 2025-01-15.
- Draft a 1-page checklist for SE handoffs (customer comms + Slack channel) — owner: Maya. Due: 2025-01-18.
- Run an internal dry-run of the runbook using a simulated spike (synthetic traffic) with Solutions Eng — schedule week of 2025-01-20.

Quick references / useful links:
- Rollout ticket: JIRA-9876 (contains activation matrix & target slices)
- Companion experiment sim: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-sim/pull/42
- Support tagging guide: confluence page (CONFLUENCE-12345)

Endnotes (tone and expectations):
This is intentionally light and iterates fast. It should live near the rollout ticket and be copied into the Console runbook for each beta. If this becomes the canonical flow, we will refine into a templated playbook with scripted alerting and a single-button rollback. For now: prefer clarity over completeness — short updates and clear stop conditions win.

----
Version history (short):
- 2025-01-10 initial draft (Sophie)
- 2025-01-12 added telemetry radar + early thresholds (Liam)
- 2025-02-02 clarified runbook snippets and stakeholder cadence (Maya)
